question.text: A guar seed producer sells 1 MT (10 quintals) of Aug futures at Rs 4,050/quintal. Spot price drops to Rs 3,950/quintal and he buys back the August futures at Rs 4,000/quintal. What is the futures profit?

explanation.text: The Logic: Futures profit per quintal = 4,050 - 4,000 = Rs 50. For 10 quintals total futures profit = Rs 500. This offsets the Rs 500 spot loss of (4,000 - 3,950) × 10. The Trap: Rs 50 is the per-quintal profit only. Rs 5,000 uses the wrong multiplier. Rs 100 miscalculates. Multiply per-unit profit by total quantity. Note: The short hedge effectively locks in Rs 4,050 - Rs 50 = Rs 4,000/quintal for the producer despite the spot decline.
